subject: English
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to the highlighted word: The general ordered his troops to halt immediately.
solution: 'Halt' means to stop; its opposite is to continue or proceed. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to the highlighted word: Despite his initial reluctance, he finally acquiesced to their demands.
solution: 'Acquiesced' means agreed or accepted reluctantly; its opposite is to reject. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to the highlighted word: The monster in the story had a hideous face that frightened everyone.
solution: 'Hideous' means extremely ugly; its opposite is attractive. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to the highlighted word: After years of hard work, he finally found atonement by proving his innocence.
solution: 'Atonement' means making amends or salvation; its opposite is condemnation. Salvation is a synonym, so it is not the answer. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to the highlighted word: The two neighbours were involved in a long feud over their property boundary.
solution: 'Feud' means a prolonged bitter quarrel; its opposite is harmony. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to the highlighted word: Constant delays can vitiate the effectiveness of the entire project.
solution: 'Vitiate' means to spoil, impair or destroy the effectiveness of something; annihilate (to destroy) is the closest. Matches option A.

stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to the highlighted word: As the sun rose, we stood quietly to behold the breathtaking view.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to the highlighted word: The king entered the hall wearing a velvet robe embroidered with gold.

subject: English
stem: Arrange P, Q, R, S between S1 and S6. S1: The current debate on intellectual property rights (IPRs) raises a number of important issues concerning the strategy and policies for building a more dynamic national agricultural research system. S6: The argument was that incentives are necessary to stimulate innovations, and that this calls for a system of patents which gives innovators the sole right to use. P: TRIPs, for the first time, seeks to bring innovations in agricultural technology under a new worldwide IPR regime. Q: The agribusiness MNCs (along with pharmaceutical companies) played a leading part in lobbying for such a regime during the Uruguay Round negotiations. R: With the relative roles of public and private sectors, and the role of agribusiness multinational corporations (MNCs). S: This debate has been stimulated by the international agreement on Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPs), negotiated as part of the Uruguay Round.
solution: R completes S1's list of issues, S introduces TRIPs, P explains what TRIPs seeks to do, and Q names the MNCs that lobbied for it, leading to S6. Order RSPQ. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Arrange P, Q, R, S between S1 and S6. S1: In this genealogy, some pure lines of descent follow their logic to the inevitable point of extinction, others engage in cross-fertilization, and yet others undergo mutation to maintain their energy. S6: Uncharitable as it may sound, the history of Indian abstractionism records a series of attempts to avoid the risks of abstraction. P: It is equally possible to enumerate the troughs where the two principles do not come together, thus arriving at a very different account. Q: However, this genealogical survey demonstrates the wave at its crests at points. R: Ideas sensuously ordained rather than fabricated programmatically to a concept. S: Those points where the metaphysical and the painterly have been fused in images of abiding potency.
solution: Q introduces the crests, S defines those points where metaphysical and painterly fuse, R elaborates the nature of those ideas, and P offers the contrasting troughs. Order QSRP. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Arrange P, Q, R, S between S1 and S6. S1: The narrator of Midnight's Children describes it as a kind of collective fantasy. S6: One could argue that nation-states are a kind of collective fantasy. P: I suppose what he, or I, through him was trying to say, was that there never had been a political entity called India until 1947. Q: It was an invention of the nationalist movement. And a very successful invention. R: So it struck me that what was coming into being, this idea of a nation-state, was an invention. S: The thing that became independent had never previously existed, except that there had been an area, a zone called India.
solution: P states there was no political entity called India until 1947, S adds that what became independent had never existed, R concludes the nation-state was an invention, and Q calls it a successful invention of the nationalist movement. Order PSRQ. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Arrange P, Q, R, S between S1 and S6. S1: Not content with shaking up the multi-billion-dollar market for computer memory, some researchers have even more ambitious plans for magnetic computing. S6: Dr. Cowburn and Dr. Welland have demonstrated how a logic gate could work in such a scheme. P: Outlined research that could form the basis of a magnetic microprocessor, a chip capable of manipulating (rather than merely storing) information magnetically. Q: In a paper published last month in Science, Russell Cowburn and Mark Welland of Cambridge University. R: In place of conducting wires, a magnetic processor would have rows of magnetic dots, each of which could be polarised in one of two directions. S: Individual bits of information would travel down the rows as magnetic pulses, changing the orientation of the dots as they went.
solution: Q names the researchers, P completes the sentence by outlining their research, R describes the magnetic dots replacing wires, and S explains how bits travel down the rows. Order QPRS. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Arrange P, Q, R, S between S1 and S6. S1: From ancient times, men have believed that, under certain peculiar circumstances, life could arise spontaneously. S6: In association with Buffon, the Irish Jesuit priest John Needham declared that he could bring about at will the creation of living microbes. P: This belief was held by Aristotle, Newton and Descartes, among many others, and apparently the great William Harvey too. Q: The weight of centuries gradually disintegrated men's beliefs in the spontaneous origin of maggots and mice. R: From the ooze of rivers could come eels and from the entrails of dead bulls, bees; worms from mud, and maggots from dead meat. S: But the doctrine of spontaneous generation clung tenaciously to the question of bacterial origin.
solution: P names the believers (Aristotle, Newton, Descartes), R gives concrete examples of the belief (eels, bees, worms, maggots), Q notes that the weight of centuries eroded the belief in the spontaneous origin of maggots and mice, and S adds that the doctrine still clung to bacterial origin, leading to S6. Order PRQS. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: What can be inferred from the passage about the primary tension in India's energy policy?
optA: Balancing economic growth with energy imports
optB: Reconciling environmental commitments with energy security and socio-economic priorities
optC: Prioritizing coal-based energy over renewable sources
optD: Eliminating fossil fuel subsidies to promote green hydrogen
solution: The passage frames India's energy quest as balancing economic ambition, environmental imperatives, energy security and socio-economic (just transition) concerns. Matches option B.
context: India's quest for energy security in the 21st century is a complex interplay of economic ambition, environmental imperatives, and geopolitical strategy. With rising energy demands driven by industrialization and urbanization, India relies heavily on fossil fuels, importing over 80% of its crude oil and significant natural gas. This dependency exposes the economy to global price volatility and geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East. Concurrently, India's commitment to the Paris Agreement necessitates a rapid transition to renewable energy, with ambitious targets of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. However, scaling renewables faces hurdles like land acquisition, intermittency issues, and inadequate grid infrastructure. The push for green energy intersects with socio-economic challenges. Coal-dependent regions, such as Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, face potential economic disruption due to the shift away from coal, necessitating a just transition framework to protect livelihoods. Meanwhile, initiatives like the International Solar Alliance (ISA) position India as a global leader in renewable energy diplomacy, but domestic policy inconsistencies, such as subsidies for fossil fuels, undermine progress. The rise of green hydrogen as a potential game-changer further complicates the energy landscape, demanding significant investment and technological innovation. Geopolitically, India must navigate a multipolar world where energy is a strategic asset. Collaborations with countries like Russia and the US for energy supplies coexist with tensions over technology transfers and sanctions. The challenge lies in balancing energy sovereignty with global cooperation, ensuring that India's energy transition aligns with its developmental goals without compromising environmental or strategic autonomy.

stem: Fill in the blank with the correct discourse marker: _______, what are you doing in my room?
solution: 'Excuse me' is the appropriate marker to open a challenging or attention-getting question. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Consider the diagram of a river with sections marked A, B, C, and D (a meandering river). In which one among the following lettered areas of the diagram would erosion most likely change the shape of the riverbed?
solution: Per the marked diagram, section B lies on the outer bank of the meander bend, where the swift current erodes and reshapes the riverbed. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Depends on a river/meander diagram not present in the text; the lettered bank cannot be verified, so the option letter is a best-guess based on the outer-bank-erosion principle.

subject: Geography
stem: Where is the Mekong Delta located?
solution: The Mekong River empties into the South China Sea through its delta in southern Vietnam. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is known as uplands of delta region?
solution: The raised upland ground of a delta region is locally termed the Peh; Bils are marshes and Chars are low riverine sand islands (lowlands). Matches option C.
reviewNote: Obscure regional terminology; Bils (marshes) and Chars (sand islands) are lowlands, leaving Bhabar as the upland answer, but the exact intended term is uncertain.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: 'Majuli', the river island, is located in which one of the following rivers?
solution: Majuli, the large river island in Assam, lies in the Brahmaputra. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Brahmaputra and Indus rivers are antecedent rivers. Which one of the following may be the true definition of an antecedent drainage?
optA: Which follows the initial slope of the Himalaya
optB: Which existed before the Himalayan range came into existence
optC: Which followed the dip of rock beds of the Himalaya
optD: Which followed the strike of rock beds of the Himalaya
solution: An antecedent river predates the uplift it cuts through, maintaining its course by down-cutting as the Himalaya rose. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: A deep valley characterized by steep step-like slopes is known as:
solution: A canyon is a deep valley whose walls show step-like slopes because horizontal sedimentary strata erode differentially. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following features is the result of both erosion and deposition work of a river?
solution: An oxbow lake forms when a meander is cut off by erosion and then sealed by deposition, combining both processes. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: This river originates in the Hindu Kush mountain range and flows into the Hamoun wetlands after covering about 1,100 km. There have been serious conflicts between two neighbouring nations regarding sharing of its water. Identify the river.
solution: The Helmand rises in the Hindu Kush and drains into the Hamoun wetlands, and its waters are disputed between Afghanistan and Iran. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: In India, glacial terraces known as 'Karewas' are found in:
solution: Karewas are lacustrine-glacial terrace deposits of the Kashmir (Jhelum) Valley, famous for saffron cultivation. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Karewas — an obscure regional term; answer derived from Kashmir Valley (Jhelum) association.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Basket-of-eggs topography is related to:
solution: A field of oval, smooth drumlins gives the classic basket-of-eggs topography. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: If you want to observe moraines, eskers and outwash plains, which one of the following Union Territories would you visit?
solution: Glacial features such as moraines, eskers and outwash plains occur in the glaciated high-mountain Union Territory of Ladakh. Matches option D.

stem: In the Thar region, shifting sand dunes are locally known as:

chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which of the following statements regarding Barchan is/are correct? 1. It is a crescent-shaped mound of sand deposited by wind blowing constantly from one direction in a desert. 2. The windward side has a gentle slope and the leeward side is steep. 3. The horns of a barchan point in the direction of the wind. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: A barchan is a crescent dune with a gentle windward and steep leeward slope, and its horns trail downwind, so all three statements are correct. Matches option D.

stem: The lowest part of most bolsons is occupied by a landform called playa. Which category of landform formation does it represent?
solution: Bolsons and their central playas are depositional features of desert basins, so they are arid landforms. Matches option B.

stem: Which one of the following is NOT a coastal depositional feature?
solution: Tombolo, sand bar and spit are depositional, whereas a sea stack is an erosional remnant. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which of the following are coastal erosional features? 1. Notch 2. Sea arch 3. Cliff 4. Hook. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Notch, sea arch and cliff are wave-cut erosional forms, while a hook is a depositional spit variant. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following combinations of stalactites and stalagmites is correct?
optA: Stalactites hang from the ceiling and stalagmites hang from the floor
optB: Stalactites hang from the ceiling and stalagmites rise from the floor
optC: Stalactites rise from the floor and stalagmites hang from the ceiling
solution: Stalactites grow downward from the cave ceiling while stalagmites build upward from the floor. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Stalactite, stalagmite and pillars are depositional landforms of:
solution: These dripstone features are deposited by mineral-rich underground (ground) water in limestone caves. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: An upfold in rock is known as:
solution: An arch-shaped upfold of strata is an anticline, whereas a downfold is a syncline. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: In which one of the following folds is the axial plane virtually horizontal?
solution: A recumbent fold is over-turned so far that its axial plane lies nearly horizontal. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: A large body of magmatic material that cools at great depth in the Earth's crust and develops in the form of large domes is known as:
solution: Per NCERT, a large magmatic body cooling at great depth and forming large granitic domes is a batholith. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: The formation of 'tors' on small rocky hills is associated with:
solution: Tors are residual boulder masses produced by the weathering of jointed granite. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is the lowermost/innermost intrusive igneous body?
solution: The batholith is the deepest and largest intrusive body, forming the innermost/lowermost pluton. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is NOT an example of a fold mountain?
solution: The Alps, Andes and Rockies are fold mountains, whereas Mt. Fuji is a volcanic cone. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below: List I (Geomorphic Agent): A. Ground water, B. Running water, C. Glacier, D. Wind. List II (Feature): 1. Plunge pool, 2. Horns, 3. Playas, 4. Lapies.
solution: Ground water carves lapies, running water forms plunge pools, glaciers produce horns, and wind creates playas, giving A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3. Matches option A.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: The Defence Investiture Ceremony 2026 witnessed the presentation of Kirti Chakra, Shaurya Chakra and Vir Chakra by the President of India. The President is the:
optB: Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces
solution: Under the Constitution the President of India is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: The primary objective of the Axiom-4 Mission, in which an Indian astronaut participated, was:
optB: Conducting scientific experiments aboard the International Space Station
solution: Axiom-4 was a private crewed mission to the International Space Station whose goal was to conduct scientific experiments aboard the ISS. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Which of the following groupings is primarily associated with strategic cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region?
solution: The QUAD (India, USA, Japan and Australia) is the grouping focused on strategic cooperation in the Indo-Pacific. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Exercise Sada Tanseeq, seen in recent current affairs, is a joint military exercise between India and:
solution: Exercise Sada Tanseeq is the bilateral joint military exercise between India and Saudi Arabia. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
subtopic: Civilian Awards, Honours and Educational Institutions
stem: The Padma Awards in India are announced every year on the occasion of:
solution: The Padma Awards are announced each year on the eve of Republic Day. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem: Two popular Assemblies of the Vedic period were
solution: The two principal popular assemblies of the Vedic polity were the Sabha and the Samiti. Matches option A.

subject: History
stem: The ritualistic precepts pertaining to the hymns of the Vedas are known as the
solution: The Brahmanas are the prose texts explaining the ritualistic application of the Vedic hymns. Matches option C.

subject: History
stem: Which of the following contains the famous Gayatri Mantra?
solution: The Gayatri Mantra occurs in the third mandala of the Rigveda. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem:
The Rig-Vedic Aryans were a pastoral people is born out by the fact that
I. There are many references to the cow in the Rig-Veda
II. Most of the wars were fought for the sake of cows
III. Gifts made to priests were usually cows
optA: There are many references to the cow in the Rig-Veda
optB: Most of the wars were fought for the sake of cows
optC: Gifts made to priests were usually cows
solution: Cattle-centred references, cattle-raid wars (gavishti) and cattle as gifts all point to a pastoral society. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem: The famous Vedic river which had long ago become extinct and now supposed to be flowing underground in Rajasthan is
solution: The Saraswati is the revered Vedic river now believed to have dried up and flow underground in Rajasthan. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem: The rivers Ganga and Yamuna are mentioned for the first time in:
solution: The Ganga and Yamuna find their earliest mention in the Rigveda (the Nadistuti Sukta). Matches option D.

subject: History
stem: The famous dialogue between Nachiketa and Yama is mentioned in the:
solution: The dialogue between Nachiketa and Yama on death and the soul is recorded in the Kathopanishad. Matches option A.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the source of Vedic Civilisation:
I. The most important source of Vedic Civilisation is the Vedas.
II. The Vedas are neither any individual religious work nor a collection of a definite number of books compiled at a particular time.
III. It consists of three successive classes of literary creations.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
solution: All three statements correctly describe the Vedas as the chief source, composed over time as successive classes of literature. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the age of Vedic Civilisation:
I. Bal Gangadhar Tilak, on astronomical grounds, dated Rig Veda to 6000 B.C. to Harmon Jacobi, Vedic civilization flourished between 4500 B.C. and 2500 B.C. and the Samhitas were composed in the latter half of the period.
II. Famous Sanskritist, Winternitz felt that the Rig Veda was probably composed in the third millennium B.C.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
solution: Both statements correctly report the datings by Tilak/Jacobi and by Winternitz. Matches option C.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rig Vedic States and its territory:
I. The territory known to Vedic people was divided into a number of states-republican and monarchical.
II. The battle of ten kings, gives names of ten kings who participated in a war against Sudas who was Bharata king of Tritsus family.
III. The ten kings were of the states of Purus, Yadus, Turvasas, Anus and Druhyus along with five others viz Alinas, Pakhtas, Bhalanas, Sibis and Vishanins.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
solution: All three statements correctly describe the Vedic states and the Dasarajna (battle of ten kings) against Sudas. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the four Vedas
I. Rig-Veda is a collection of hymns
II. Samveda is a collection of songs mostly taken from Rig Veda
III. Atharvaveda is a collection of sacrificial formulae
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
solution: I and II are correct; III is wrong because sacrificial formulae belong to the Yajurveda while the Atharvaveda is a collection of magical spells and charms. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem: Which of the correct ascending order of Political structure of Rig Vedic India?
solution: The ascending Vedic political units run Kula (family), Grama (village), Vis (clan), Jana (tribe) and Rashtra (kingdom). Matches option B.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statement regarding the Brahamana text of Vedic Civilisation:
I. The Brahamanas are the collection of ancient Vedic texts with commentaries on the hymns of the four Vedas.
II. The Brahamanas contain details about the meaning of Vedic hymns, their applications, stories of their origins, etc.
III. Chandogya Brahmana, one of the oldest Brahmana, includes eight suktas (hymns) for the ceremony of marriage and rituals at the birth of a child.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
solution: All three statements correctly describe the Brahmanas and the marriage/birth hymns of the Chandogya (Mantra) Brahmana. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the "Vedas":
I. The word 'Veda' signifies knowledge and they are actually providing humans with knowledge to conduct their life on Earth.
II. The Vedas were initially handed down orally by generations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Both statements are correct: Veda means knowledge and the texts were transmitted orally across generations before being written. Matches option C.

subject: History
stem: Which of the following text is contemporary to Vedas?
solution: The Zend Avesta, the Iranian scripture closely related in language and content to the Rigveda, is contemporary to the Vedas. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem: The ninth mandala of the Rigveda samhita is devoted wholly to:
optC: Gods related to plants and drugs
optD: 'Soma' and the god who is named after the drink
solution: The ninth mandala of the Rigveda is dedicated entirely to Soma Pavamana, the deified sacred drink. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem: Which one of the following stages of the life of man in Aryan Society, in ascending order of age, is correct?
solution: The four ashramas in order of increasing age are Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sanyasa. Matches option C.

subject: History
stem: The Aryans succeeded in their conflicts with the pre-Aryans because:
optA: they used elephants on a large scale
optB: they used chariots driven by horses
optD: they were from an advanced urban culture
solution: The Aryans' advantage lay in their swift horse-drawn chariots. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem: Which one of the following is INCORRECTLY matched?
optA: Yajur Veda- knowledge of the sacrificial formulas
optB: Atharva Veda- knowledge of the magic formulas
optC: Rig Veda- knowledge of the Hymns of Praise
solution: The Sama Veda is the knowledge of melodies and chants, not of science, so this pairing is incorrect. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem: Which of the following is false as per Vedic theory?
optA: The Kshatriyas, or warrior rulers, came from Purusha's arms
optB: The Vaishyas, or the commoners, came from Purusha's thighs
optC: The Brahmans, or priests, came from Purusha's ears
optD: The Shudras, or laborers and servants, came from Purusha's feet
solution: Per the Purusha Sukta the Brahmans emerged from the mouth of Purusha, not the ears, so this statement is false. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: The correct relation between the radius of curvature \(R\) and focal length \(f\) of a spherical mirror is
solution: For a spherical mirror the focus lies midway between the pole and the centre of curvature, so the focal length is half the radius of curvature: \(f = \frac{R}{2}\), i.e. \(R = 2f\). Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: In case of a concave mirror, if an object is kept between principal focus \(F\) and pole \(P\) of the mirror, then which one of the following statements about the image is NOT correct?
optB: The image will be enlarged or magnified
optC: The image will be formed at infinity
solution: For a concave mirror with the object between \(F\) and \(P\), the image is virtual, erect, enlarged and formed behind the mirror. An image at infinity is produced only when the object is exactly at the focus, not between \(F\) and \(P\). Hence the statement that is NOT correct is that the image is formed at infinity. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: A lens has a power of \(+2.0\) Dioptre. Which one of the following statements about the lens is true?
optA: The lens is concave and has a focal length of \(0.5\) metre
optB: The lens is convex and has a focal length of \(2.0\) metre
optC: The lens is convex and has a focal length of \(0.5\) metre
optD: The lens is concave and has a focal length of \(2.0\) metre
solution: Power \(P = \frac{1}{f}\) with \(f\) in metres. A positive power means a converging (convex) lens. Here \(f = \frac{1}{P} = \frac{1}{2.0} = 0.5\) metre. So the lens is convex with focal length \(0.5\) metre. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Spherical mirror formula relating an object distance \(u\), image distance \(v\) and focal length of mirror \(f\) may be applied to a plane mirror when
solution: A plane mirror is the limiting case of a spherical mirror with infinite radius of curvature, hence infinite focal length. Putting \(f \to \infty\) in \(\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\) gives \(\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=0\), i.e. \(v=-u\): the image is as far behind as the object is in front, exactly as for a plane mirror. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: A rectangle ABCD is kept in front of a concave mirror of focal length \(f\) with its corners A and B being, respectively, at distances \(2f\) and \(3f\) from the mirror with AB along the principal axis as shown in the figure. It forms an image A'B'C'D' in front of the mirror. What is the ratio of B'C' to A'D'?
solution: AD is the vertical side at object distance \(u=2f\) (the centre of curvature). Here \(\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{2f}=\frac{1}{2f}\), so \(v=2f\) and lateral magnification \(m_A=-\frac{v}{u}=-1\); thus \(A'D'\) has the same height as \(AD\). BC is the vertical side at \(u=3f\): \(\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{3f}=\frac{2}{3f}\), so \(v=\frac{3f}{2}\) and \(m_B=-\frac{v}{u}=-\frac{3f/2}{3f}=-\frac{1}{2}\); thus \(B'C'\) is half the height of \(BC\). Since \(AD\) and \(BC\) are equal sides of the rectangle, \(\frac{B'C'}{A'D'}=\frac{1}{2}\). Matches option C.
reviewNote: Figure did not extract. Assumed rectangle with AB along the principal axis, A at 2f and B at 3f, and the vertical sides AD (at A) and BC (at B) of equal height so their images can be compared by lateral magnification.

subject: Physics
stem: Two plane mirrors XY and YZ (XY perpendicular to YZ) are joined at their edge. A light ray falls on one of the mirrors and is reflected back parallel to its original path. The two mirrors are now rotated together by an angle \(\theta\) to their new position X'YZ', and the new reflected ray is at an angle \(\alpha\) from the original reflected ray. Then:
solution: Two mutually perpendicular mirrors act as a retroreflector: after two successive reflections the emergent ray is always antiparallel to the incident ray, independent of how the rigid mirror pair is oriented. Rotating the whole assembly by theta therefore does not change the direction of the returned ray, so the new reflected ray stays parallel to the original one and alpha = 0. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: Sita, \(1.5\) m high, stands before a plane mirror fixed on a wall to view her full image. What should be the minimum height of the plane mirror so that Sita can view her image fully?
solution: To see one's full image in a plane mirror, the mirror need only be half the person's height (a consequence of the law of reflection, independent of the distance from the mirror). Minimum height \(=\frac{1.5}{2}=0.75\) m. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: The mirrors used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles are
solution: Rear-view mirrors are convex because a convex mirror always forms an erect, diminished image and provides a wider field of view, letting the driver see a larger area behind the vehicle. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: An object is placed far beyond the centre of curvature of a concave mirror and starts accelerating towards the mirror. Which one is correct?
optA: The image will accelerate towards the centre of curvature.
optB: The image will accelerate towards the focus.
optC: The image will accelerate towards the pole of the mirror.
optD: The image will move with a constant speed towards the focus.
solution: For a concave mirror, when the object is at infinity the image lies at the focus \(F\); when the object reaches the centre of curvature \(C\) the image is also at \(C\). So as the object moves from far away towards the mirror, its real image travels from \(F\) outward towards \(C\). Hence the image moves towards the centre of curvature. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: Concave mirror is used in headlights of vehicles, because it
optA: focuses light from the bulb onto nearby vehicles
optC: fits well into the shape of the headlight
solution: In a headlight the bulb is placed at the focus of the concave mirror. Rays coming from the focus, after reflection, emerge parallel to the principal axis, producing a strong parallel beam that travels a long distance. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the following is the natural phenomenon based on which a simple periscope works?
solution: A simple periscope uses two plane mirrors inclined at 45 degrees; light is turned twice by ordinary reflection at these mirrors. Hence it works on the reflection of light. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the following statements is correct for a plane mirror?
optB: The size of the image of an object placed in front of the mirror is slightly less than that of the object.
optC: The image is virtual, erect and laterally inverted.
solution: A plane mirror forms an image that is virtual, erect, of the same size as the object and laterally inverted, located as far behind the mirror as the object is in front. Its focal length is infinite (not zero or 200 cm), and the image is the same size, not smaller. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: An object is placed between infinity and the pole \(P\) of a convex mirror. The position of the image is
optA: between pole \(P\) and the focus \(F\), behind the mirror
optB: between the focus \(F\) and infinity, behind the mirror
optC: between the pole \(P\) and the infinity, in front of the mirror
optD: at the focus \(F\), behind the mirror
solution: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image located behind the mirror. As the object moves from infinity to the pole, the image moves from the focus \(F\) to the pole \(P\); thus for any object between infinity and \(P\) the image lies between \(P\) and \(F\) behind the mirror. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: The refractive index of fused quartz is \(1.46\) and that of sapphire is \(1.77\). If \(v_q\) is the speed of light in quartz and \(v_s\) is the speed of light in sapphire, then which one of the following relations is correct?
solution: The speed of light in a medium is \(v=\frac{c}{n}\), so a smaller refractive index means a larger speed. Since quartz (\(n=1.46\)) has a smaller index than sapphire (\(n=1.77\)), light travels faster in quartz: \(v_q > v_s\). Matches option A.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: If the absolute refractive indices of glass and water are \(\frac{3}{2}\) and \(\frac{4}{3}\) respectively, what will be the ratio of velocity of light in glass and water?
solution: Since \(v=\frac{c}{n}\), the ratio \(\frac{v_{glass}}{v_{water}}=\frac{n_{water}}{n_{glass}}=\frac{4/3}{3/2}=\frac{4}{3}\times\frac{2}{3}=\frac{8}{9}\). So the ratio is \(8:9\). Matches option D.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: The refractive indices of two media are denoted by \(n_1\) and \(n_2\), and the velocities of light in these two media are respectively \(v_1\) and \(v_2\). If \(\frac{n_2}{n_1}\) is \(1.5\), which one of the following statements is correct?
solution: For each medium \(v=\frac{c}{n}\), so \(\frac{v_1}{v_2}=\frac{n_2}{n_1}=1.5\). Therefore \(v_1 = 1.5\,v_2\). Matches option A.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: Light waves are incident on an air-glass boundary. Some of the light waves are reflected and some are refracted in the glass. Which one of the following properties is the same for the incident wave and the refracted wave?
solution: On refraction the frequency of light does not change because it is fixed by the source; only the speed and wavelength change as the medium changes, and the direction bends. Hence frequency is the same for the incident and refracted waves. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: If a ray of light enters from a rarer medium to a denser medium at zero angle of incidence, it would
solution: At normal (zero angle of) incidence the ray travels along the normal. By Snell's law \(n_1\sin i = n_2\sin r\), with \(i=0\) we get \(r=0\), so there is no bending and the ray goes straight into the denser medium. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: Mirage is an illustration of
optC: only total internal reflection of light.
optD: both refraction and total internal reflection of light.
solution: In a mirage, layers of air near hot ground have progressively smaller refractive index, so light from the sky bends continuously (refraction) and eventually undergoes total internal reflection, making the ground look like a reflecting pool. It thus involves both refraction and total internal reflection. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: The refractive index of crown glass is close to \(\frac{3}{2}\). If the speed of light in air is \(c\), then the speed of light in the crown glass will be close to
solution: The speed of light in a medium is \(v=\frac{c}{n}=\frac{c}{3/2}=\frac{2}{3}c\). Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: A periscope uses two plane mirrors at \(45^\circ\). If the tube is filled with a transparent liquid of refractive index \(1.5\), which one is correct regarding the image?
optB: The image will appear laterally shifted.
optC: The image will appear \(1.5\) times brighter.
optD: The image will appear \(1.5\) times darker.
solution: The two plane mirrors turn the light purely by reflection, which is independent of the medium filling the tube, so the image remains unchanged. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: A glass slab (refractive index \(1.5\)) is cut as a parallelogram ABCD with BC polished as a reflector. Light travelling inside the glass is incident on face AB at \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) (measured from the normal to AB). Which angle \(\angle ABC = \theta\) causes the reflected light to retrace its path?
solution: From the slab geometry in the figure, retracing the path requires the ray to strike the polished face BC along its normal; solving the triangle gives the interior angle ABC = theta = pi/6. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Figure did not extract. Assumed the stated angle is the internal ray's angle with the normal to face AB, and that retrace requires normal incidence on the polished face BC; the refractive index is not needed for the geometry.

subject: Physics
stem: The radii of curvature of the faces of a double convex lens are \(10\) cm and \(20\) cm. The refractive index of the glass is \(1.5\). What is the power of this lens (in units of dioptre)?
solution: By the lensmaker's formula for a double convex lens, \(\frac{1}{f}=(n-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}+\frac{1}{R_2}\right)\). Working in centimetres, \(\frac{1}{f}=(1.5-1)\left(\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{20}\right)=0.5\times\frac{3}{20}=\frac{3}{40}\,\text{cm}^{-1}\), so \(f=\frac{40}{3}\approx13.33\) cm \(=0.1333\) m. Power \(P=\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{0.1333}=+7.5\) D. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The compound \(C_6H_{12}O_4\) contains
optB: twice the mass percent of H as compared to the mass percent of C
optC: six times the mass percent of C as compared to the mass percent of H
optD: thrice the mass percent of H as compared to the mass percent of O
solution: Molar mass of \(C_6H_{12}O_4\) = 6(12)+12(1)+4(16) = 72+12+64 = 148 g. Mass percent of C = 72/148 = 48.6 percent; mass percent of H = 12/148 = 8.1 percent. Ratio 48.6/8.1 = 6, so C is six times the mass percent of H. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The proposition 'equal volumes of different gases contain equal numbers of molecules at the same temperature and pressure' is known as
solution: Equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules is Avogadro's hypothesis. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Equal volume of all gases, when measured at the same temperature and pressure, contain an equal number of particles. Who proposed the above law?
solution: The law of equal numbers of particles in equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure was proposed by Amedeo Avogadro. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The mass of 0.5 mole of \(N_2\) gas is
solution: Molar mass of \(N_2\) = 28 g/mol. Mass = 0.5 mol x 28 g/mol = 14 g. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
optA: Half mole of nitrogen gas is measured 11.2 liter at STP
optB: 17 gram of ammonia gas contains \(6.022 \times 10^{23}\) molecules at STP
optC: 22.4 litre of \(CO_2\) gas at STP contains 44 gram of molecules
optD: 4 gram of hydrogen gas contains \(6.022 \times 10^{23}\) molecules
solution: 4 g of \(H_2\) (molar mass 2 g/mol) equals 2 moles, which contains 2 x 6.022 x 10^23 molecules, not 6.022 x 10^23; so (d) is incorrect. (a) 0.5 mol N2 = 11.2 L at STP, (b) 17 g NH3 = 1 mol = 6.022 x 10^23 molecules, and (c) 22.4 L CO2 = 1 mol = 44 g are all correct. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which is the correct IUPAC name of the compound \(CH_3\text{-}CH=CH\text{-}COOH\)?
solution: A 4-carbon chain with COOH (C1), a double bond between C2 and C3 gives but-2-enoic acid (carboxyl carbon is C1). Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which is the correct name of \(CH_3\text{-}CH_2\text{-}O\text{-}CH_2\text{-}CH_3\)?
solution: This ether has two ethyl groups; the IUPAC name treats the larger chain as ethane with an ethoxy substituent, giving ethoxyethane. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The correct IUPAC name of \(CH_3\text{-}CH(CH_3)\text{-}CH(OH)\text{-}CH_3\) is
solution: Longest chain is 4 carbons (butane). Numbering to give OH the lower locant places OH at C2 and the methyl branch at C3, giving 3-methylbutan-2-ol. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which is the correct IUPAC name of \(CH_2=CH\text{-}CH(Cl)\text{-}CH_3\)?
solution: Numbering from the double-bond end gives the C=C at C1 and the Cl at C3, so the name is 3-chlorobut-1-ene. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The IUPAC name of \(CH_3\text{-}CO\text{-}CH_2\text{-}CH_3\) is
solution: A 4-carbon ketone with the carbonyl at C2 is butan-2-one, i.e. 2-butanone (the locant specifies the carbonyl position). Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which is the correct IUPAC name of \(C_6H_5\text{-}CH_2\text{-}CH_2\text{-}OH\)?
solution: A two-carbon chain bearing OH at C1 and a phenyl group at C2 is 2-phenylethanol (option (b) prints it as 2-Phenyleethanol). Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The IUPAC name of \(CH_3\text{-}CH_2\text{-}CH(Br)\text{-}CH_2\text{-}CH_3\) is
solution: The 5-carbon chain (pentane) carries Br on the central carbon C3, giving 3-bromopentane. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which is the correct IUPAC name of \(CH_3\text{-}C{\equiv}C\text{-}CH_2\text{-}CH_3\)?
solution: A 5-carbon chain with a triple bond starting at C2 is pent-2-yne (current IUPAC places the locant before the suffix -yne). Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The IUPAC name of \(CH_2=CH\text{-}CH=CH_2\) is
solution: A 4-carbon chain with double bonds at C1 and C3 is buta-1,3-diene (current IUPAC form with locants before -diene). Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following is the correct name of \(CH_3\text{-}CH=CH\text{-}CH_2\text{-}CH_3\)?
solution: A 5-carbon chain with the double bond at C2, written in current IUPAC style with the locant before the suffix, is pent-2-ene. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The IUPAC name of \((CH_3)_2CH\text{-}CH_2\text{-}CH(CH_3)\text{-}CH_3\) is
solution: The longest chain is 5 carbons (pentane) with methyl branches at C2 and C4, giving 2,4-dimethylpentane. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which is the correct IUPAC name of \(CH_3\text{-}CH(CH_3)\text{-}CH_2\text{-}CH_3\)?
solution: The longest chain is 4 carbons (butane) with a methyl branch at C2 (lower locant), giving 2-methylbutane. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Fullerene \(C_{70}\) is made up of how many pentagons and hexagons?
solution: Every closed fullerene has exactly 12 pentagons; C70 has 25 hexagons (compared with 20 in C60). Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Fullerene \(C_{60}\) has how many fused five-membered rings?
solution: Buckminsterfullerene C60 consists of 12 five-membered (pentagonal) rings and 20 six-membered rings. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which compound is a ring-chain isomer of hex-1-ene?
solution: Hex-1-ene has formula \(C_6H_{12}\). Its ring-chain isomer must share this formula; cyclohexane is \(C_6H_{12}\). Matches option C.
reviewNote: Both cyclohexane (C6H12) and methylcyclopentane (C6H12) are ring-chain isomers of hex-1-ene; cyclohexane is the intended straight-ring answer.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which pair are position isomers?
solution: Position isomers differ only in the position of a substituent or functional group on the same carbon skeleton. 1-Bromopropane and 2-bromopropane differ only in the position of Br. Matches option A.
reviewNote: 1-Butene vs 2-butene (option c) are also position isomers; option (a) is the intended answer as the clearest positional pair with a single substituent.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which pair of compounds are positional isomers?
solution: 1-Propanol and 2-propanol have the same skeleton and functional group (OH), differing only in the position of OH, making them positional isomers. n-Butane/isobutane are chain isomers, propene/cyclopropane are ring-chain isomers, and ethanol/dimethyl ether are functional isomers. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which pair of compounds are chain isomers?
solution: Chain isomers differ in the branching of the carbon skeleton. n-Butane (straight chain) and isobutane (branched) are chain isomers of \(C_4H_{10}\). Matches option A.

subject: Biology
stem: Who among the following shared the Nobel Prize in 1962 along with Francis Crick and James Watson for their discoveries concerning the molecular structure of nucleic acids?
solution: The 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was shared by Francis Crick, James Watson and Maurice Wilkins. Matches option B.

subject: Biology
stem: Different varieties of the same gene are called
solution: Alternative forms (varieties) of the same gene occupying the same locus are called alleles. Matches option C.

subject: Biology
stem: Which is the correct base pairing found in a normal DNA molecule?
solution: In DNA, complementary base pairing follows Chargaff's rule: adenine pairs with thymine (two hydrogen bonds) and guanine pairs with cytosine. Matches option A.

subject: Biology
stem: The book The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection was authored by
solution: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection (1859) was written by Charles Darwin. Matches option A.
